chapter: Teaching, the 1951 Big Show and New York nights
title: TV work and the Terry Gibbs band
summary: Troup's job led to recordings and TV shows, including the Terry Gibbs band on Operation Entertainment, whose sax section became Supersax.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: But no more. It was just that's out, you know. But as I say this was very rewarding, being with Bobby, and getting a chance to play, and getting the exposure. And consequently as I said I did quite a few recordings, and I got into quite a bit of TV work as a result of that. I did the Lucy Show, and the Bill Cosby Show, This is Your Life, I did another show with Terry Gibby's band, oh, a great band. For two years we did a show called Operation Entertainment. And that -- the band actually the saxophone section was like -- is what we know now as supersax. That was our saxophone section.
Yeah, yeah. Oh, it was a great band, it was a fun band. It's -- and for two years it was just a

real pleasure, and I'm still working with Bobby and we would go out for 10 days, and Joe Pass would sub for me and Al Viola, and when I came back it was my job. They had to leave. But that band was Med Flory, Jack Magliori, Joe Lopes, everybody that's in --
Yes. Well, Warren was there for a while. But the nucleus -- and Buddy Clark.
